description: Guide a student to synthesize multiple alpha sources into a single composite signal. The student should construct at least three signals from distinct sources such as trend, mean reversion, cross-asset relative value, and carry from funding rates, analyze correlations between them, combine them using a stated method, evaluate the composite signal, compare it against the individual signals, and discuss when diversification fails.

student_openings.beginner_no_finance: I've been learning about different trading signals - some follow trends, others bet on reversals. Can I combine them to get something better than either one alone?
student_openings.intermediate_developer: I want to build a multi-signal alpha model for BTC. I have price data, ETH for cross-asset analysis, and funding rate data. How do I systematically combine multiple signals and evaluate the composite?
student_openings.advanced_quant: I'm constructing a multi-factor alpha model for crypto futures. I want to combine orthogonal signal sources - time-series momentum, mean-reversion, cross-asset relative value, and carry from funding rate - with IC-weighted combination. I need to evaluate diversification benefit and tail correlation.

ground_truth.expected_outcome: Student produces a research output containing: (1) at least three individual signals from distinct alpha sources, (2) signal-to-signal correlation analysis, (3) a composite signal built with an explicit combination method, (4) evaluation of the composite versus the individual signals, (5) quantitative evidence that the composite improves IC IR or Sharpe versus the best single signal, and (6) discussion of when diversification fails, such as correlated drawdowns or regime shifts.
required_capabilities: Construct multiple individual signals from distinct alpha sources
Analyze signal-to-signal correlations to assess diversification potential
Combine signals using a principled method
Evaluate the composite signal and compare it against the individual signals
Discuss the limits of diversification under correlated drawdowns or regime shifts
